passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: The following discussion and analysis is intended to provide the reader with information that will assist in understanding the significant factors affecting our consolidated operating results, financial condition, liquidity, and capital resources during the two-year period ended December 27, 2025 (our fiscal years 2025 and 2024). For a comparison of our results of operations for fiscal year December 28, 2024 and December 30, 2023, see “Part II, Item 7. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 28, 2024, filed with the SEC on February 20, 2025. This discussion should be read in conjunction with our Consolidated Financial Statements and Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements included elsewhere in this report. This discussion contains forward-looking statements and information. See “Forward-Looking Statements and Information” and “Risk Factors” included elsewhere in this report. Tractor Supply reports its financial results in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (“U.S. GAAP”). Tractor Supply also uses certain non-GAAP measures that fall within the meaning of Securities and Exchange Commission Regulation G and Regulation S-K Item 10(e), which may provide users of the financial information with additional meaningful comparison to prior reported results. Non-GAAP measures do not have standardized definitions and are not defined by U.S. GAAP. Therefore, Tractor Supply’s non-GAAP measures are unlikely to be comparable to similar measures presented by other companies. The presentation of these non-GAAP measures should not be considered in isolation from, as a substitute for, or as superior to the financial information presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP. We believe this information is useful in providing period-to-period comparisons of the results of our continuing operations. Overview Founded in 1938, Tractor Supply Company (the “Company” or “Tractor Supply” or “we” or “our” or “us”) is the largest rural lifestyle retailer in the United States (“U.S.”). The Company is focused on supplying the needs of recreational farmers, ranchers, and all those who enjoy living the rural lifestyle (which we refer to as the “ Out Here ” lifestyle). As of December 27, 2025, we operated 2,602 retail stores in 49 states under the names Tractor Supply Company and Petsense by Tractor Supply. Our stores are located primarily in towns outlying major metropolitan markets and in rural communities. We also operate websites under the names TractorSupply.com, Petsense.com , and Allivet.com as well as a Tractor Supply Company mobile application. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: Our business faces many risks. Certain risks of which we are currently aware and deem to be material are described below. If any of the events or circumstances described in the following risk factors occur, our business, financial condition or results of operations may significantly suffer, and the trading price of our common stock could decline. These risk factors should be read in conjunction with the other information in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Strategic and Competitive Risks We may be unable to increase sales at our existing stores. We experience fluctuations in our comparable store sales at our existing stores, defined as sales in stores which have been open for at least twelve months. See Item 7. “Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” for a further discussion of comparable store sales. Various factors affect the comparable store sales at our existing stores, including, among others, the general retail sales environment, our ability to efficiently source and distribute products, global supply chain disruptions, changes in our merchandise assortment, competition, proximity of our locations to one another or to the locations of other competing retailers, increased presence of online retailers, current economic conditions, customer satisfaction with our products, retail pricing, the timing of promotional events, the release of new merchandise, the success of marketing programs, weather conditions, and our ability to attract and retain qualified team members. These factors may cause the comparable store sales results at our existing stores to differ materially from prior periods and from expectations. Past comparable store sales are not an indication of future results, and there can be no assurance that our comparable store sales will not decrease in the future. 10 Table of Contents Our merchandising and marketing initiatives may not provide expected results. We believe our past performance has been based upon, and future success will depend in part upon, the ability to develop and execute merchandising initiatives with effective marketing programs. These merchandising initiatives and marketing programs may not deliver expected results, and there is no assurance that we will correctly identify and respond in a timely manner to evolving trends and consumer preferences and expectations. If we misjudge the market or our marketing programs are not successful, we may overstock unpopular products and be forced to take inventory impairment or retail price reductions that have a material adverse effect on our profitability. Failure to execute and promote such initiatives in a timely manner could harm our ability to grow the business and could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations and financial condition. Shortages of key merchandise could also have a material adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operations. We may not timely identify or effectively respond to consumer needs, expectations, or trends, which could adversely affect our relationship with customers, the demand for our products and services, and our market share. credit_strengths.text: Tractor Supply carries minimal funded debt against a large EBITDA proxy, with gross leverage far below the consumer discretionary sector median and materially reduced year over year as long-term borrowings were repaid. The rural lifestyle retail franchise generates ample internal cash, so the balance sheet is effectively net cash after deducting unrestricted cash.

Operating cash flow comfortably funds capital expenditure and shareholder distributions combined, and covers dividends and buybacks individually with wide headroom. Free cash flow alone exceeds dividends and buybacks separately, though not their sum, so distributions lean partly on balance-sheet capacity rather than recurring free cash flow.

key_risks.text: The disclosed risk factors flag dependence on comparable store sales at existing stores, which fluctuate with the retail environment, weather, competition and online retailers. With revenue growth modest and operating margin below the sector median, a sales shortfall would pressure profitability given fixed store costs across the rural footprint.

Merchandising misjudgement is a concrete disclosed risk: unsuccessful marketing or assortment decisions could force inventory impairment or price reductions, hitting profitability. Separately, the debt note shows only long-term borrowings with no tagged short-term facilities, so reported debt may understate total borrowings if commercial paper exists untagged.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is exceptionally strong and well above the sector median, though it eased year over year as operating income stayed flat while interest expense rose. EBITDA coverage similarly exceeds the sector median by a wide margin, indicating ample capacity to absorb higher borrowing costs without impairing debt service.

Cash flow to debt and free cash flow to debt both sit far above sector medians and improved sharply year over year as borrowings fell. The current ratio exceeds the sector median but declined from the prior year, and liquidity remains adequate given the modest maturity profile disclosed.

overall_credit_view.text: The indicative financial risk profile is minimal, anchored by net cash and negligible leverage. Operating margin trails the sector median and narrowed year over year, so the credit view rests on balance-sheet strength and cash generation rather than margin leadership; continued store growth and distributions should be funded comfortably.

Analyst judgement: the issuer is well positioned to refinance or repay its modest long-term borrowings from internal cash, with no near-term maturity concentration disclosed. The main watch items are comparable store sales softness and the gap between free cash flow and total shareholder distributions, which could require periodic incremental borrowing.

credit_strengths.text: Tractor Supply 相對於龐大嘅 EBITDA 代理指標，僅背負極少計息債務，總槓桿遠低於非必需消費品行業中位數，並因償還長期借款而按年大幅下降。呢個鄉郊生活零售特許經營產生充裕嘅內部現金，因此扣除未受限現金後，資產負債表實際上係淨現金。
營運現金流足以輕鬆同時支付資本開支同股東分派，並可分別覆蓋股息同回購，且留有寬裕緩衝。單計自由現金流已超過股息同回購各自嘅金額，但不足以覆蓋兩者之和，因此分派部分依賴資產負債表能力，而非經常性自由現金流。

key_risks.text: 披露嘅風險因素指出，業務依賴現有店舖嘅同店銷售，而呢啲銷售會隨零售環境、天氣、競爭同網上零售商而波動。由於收入增長溫和，且經營利潤率低於行業中位數，一旦銷售不達預期，喺鄉郊網絡嘅固定店舖成本下，將對盈利能力構成壓力。
商品策劃失誤係一項具體嘅已披露風險：營銷或商品組合決策不成功，可能迫使存貨減值或降價，打擊盈利能力。另外，債務附註僅顯示長期借款，並無標記短期融資安排，因此若存在未標記嘅商業票據，所報告嘅債務可能低估總借款。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率異常強勁，遠高於行業中位數，儘管年內因經營收入持平而利息支出上升，覆蓋率按年有所緩和。EBITDA 覆蓋率同樣大幅超過行業中位數，顯示有充裕能力吸收更高借貸成本而不損害債務償付。
現金流對債務比率同自由現金流對債務比率均遠高於行業中位數，並因借款減少而按年大幅改善。流動比率高於行業中位數，但較上一年下降；鑑於披露嘅到期結構溫和，流動性仍然充足。

overall_credit_view.text: 指示性財務風險狀況為極低，以淨現金同微不足道嘅槓桿為錨。經營利潤率落後於行業中位數並按年收窄，因此信貸觀點建基於資產負債表實力同現金產生能力，而非利潤率領先地位；持續嘅店舖增長同分派應可輕鬆獲得資金。
分析師判斷：發行人具備良好條件，可從內部現金為其溫和嘅長期借款再融資或償還，且未披露短期到期集中情況。主要觀察事項為同店銷售疲軟，以及自由現金流與股東分派總額之間嘅差距，呢個差距可能需要定期增量借款。
